articles.title: Sismo Junín: IGP evalúa posibles daños tras el movimiento telúrico
articles.summary: Un sismo de magnitud 6,7 se registró en la región Junín, a 129 kilómetros de profundidad, informó el IGP. Su jefe, Hernando Tavera, explicó que la profundidad del evento atenuó el sacudimiento del suelo y señaló que todavía se recopila información sobre posibles daños.
articles.body_text: Un sismo de magnitud 6,7 se registró la noche de este viernes 20 de noviembre en la región Junín, informó el Centro Sismológico Nacional del Instituto Geofísico del Perú (IGP). El movimiento telúrico ocurrió a 129 kilómetros de profundidad y tuvo como referencia una ubicación a 30 kilómetros al noroeste de Junín. Hasta el momento, las autoridades no han confirmado información sobre posibles daños. En declaraciones a Latina Noticias, Hernando Tavera, jefe del IGP, indicó que la institución se encuentra recopilando información para determinar si el movimiento telúrico ocasionó afectaciones en la zona. “Estamos tratando de conseguir información sobre posibles daños que se han presentado, pero aún no tenemos información. Estamos recolectando información y vamos a ir informando en paralelo”, señaló. De acuerdo con el reporte sísmico IGP/CENSIS/RS 2026-0818, el temblor se produjo a las 7:09:19 p.m. de este viernes 20 de noviembre. El epicentro fue localizado a 30 kilómetros al noroeste de Junín, en la provincia y región del mismo nombre, y alcanzó una intensidad de V en Junín. Tavera también explicó las diferencias entre este movimiento telúrico y los sismos registrados en julio en la región. Precisó que uno de los principales factores es la profundidad a la que se originan los eventos sísmicos. Según detalló, el sismo de julio ocurrió a una profundidad de aproximadamente 9 kilómetros y cerca de las zonas urbanas de Chupaca, lo que provocó daños estructurales y el colapso de viviendas construidas con adobe. En cambio, el movimiento registrado este viernes tuvo una profundidad de 129 kilómetros. Aunque alcanzó una magnitud mayor, el sacudimiento del suelo fue menos intenso debido a la distancia entre el punto de origen del sismo y la superficie. “En este caso, el factor profundidad ha sido importante para atenuar un poco el nivel de sacudimiento que podía haberse producido”, explicó el jefe del IGP. La institución continuará recopilando información sobre las posibles consecuencias del movimiento telúrico y comunicará los resultados de su evaluación.

articles.title: Sismo de magnitud 6.7 se registró este viernes en Junín y se sintió en diferentes regiones del país, entre ellas Lima
articles.summary: Sismo de magnitud 6.7 se registró este viernes en Junín y se sintió en diferentes regiones del país, entre ellas Lima
articles.body_text: Un sismo de magnitud 6.7 se registró este viernes 20 de noviembre en el departamento de Junín, informó el Instituto Geofísico del Perú (IGP) en sus canales oficiales. De acuerdo con dicha institución, el temblor ocurrió a las 7:09 p.m. y su epicentro se localizó a 30 kilómetros al noroeste del citado departamento del centro del país. El sismo tuvo una profundidad de 129 kilómetros y una intensidad máxima de V en Junín. Según reportaron corresponsales de Canal N, el temblor de magnitud 6.7 fue percibido también en lugares como Oxapampa y Pasco. También se sintió en Lima, la capital del país. El jefe del IGP, Hernando Tavera, explicó que el temblor fue percibido con fuerza en diferentes regiones debido a su profundidad de 129 kilómetros. “Es un sismo de profundidad intermedia, por lo que el rayo de percepción del sacudimiento ha sido bastante grande y la duración ha sido un poquito larga por el paso del mayor número de ondas que se genera por ese nivel de profundidad”, indicó en diálogo con RPP. El Centro de Operaciones de Emergencia Nacional (COEN) informó en la red social ‘X’ que el movimiento telúrico fue percibido entre moderado y fuerte por la población de Junín. La entidad realiza el trabajo de monitoreo en zonas vulnerables. Por su parte, el Ministerio de Salud detalló que realiza el monitoreo de daños tras el temblor a través del COES Salud y el EMED de la Diresa de Junín. Las autoridades locales y de Defensa Civil no han reportado hasta el momento la ocurrencia de daños materiales o personales tras el fuerte sismo de magnitud 6.7.

articles.title: Precio del GNV, GLP, diésel y gasolina en Perú hoy, viernes 20 de noviembre: ¿cuánto cuesta llenar el tanque?
articles.summary: Comas registra gasohol regular desde S/18,56 por galón, mientras el premium alcanza los S/27,99 en locales de La Molina. Revisa las referencias de este miércoles y cómo consultar el precio del GNV, GLP y diésel antes de abastecer tu vehículo.
articles.body_text: Los conductores que tienen previsto abastecer sus vehículos este viernes 20 de noviembre de 2026 pueden encontrar diferencias importantes en los precios de los combustibles, incluso entre estaciones de servicio de un mismo distrito. La información reportada en la plataforma Facilito de Osinergmin permite comparar los precios del gasohol regular y premium, el diésel, el GLP y el GNV, una herramienta útil para organizar el presupuesto y evitar pagar de más al llenar el tanque. El gasohol regular presentó una diferencia considerable entre establecimientos de Lima. En Comas, los precios reportados oscilaron entre S/ 18,56 y S/ 23,49 por galón; mientras que en Lurigancho se ubicaron entre S/ 18,79 y S/ 22,76. También destacaron Breña, con tarifas desde S/ 19,15, y San Juan de Lurigancho, donde el valor mínimo fue de S/ 19,39. Esta variación puede representar un ahorro importante para quienes utilizan el vehículo a diario. Por ejemplo, una diferencia de S/ 5 por galón equivale a S/ 60 en una carga de 12 galones. Por ello, antes de dirigirse a un grifo, conviene revisar qué establecimientos cercanos ofrecen las tarifas más convenientes. Para el gasohol premium, los registros mostraron precios desde S/ 20,39 por galón en Ate. En otros distritos, como Villa El Salvador y Jesús María, las tarifas mínimas fueron de S/ 20,79. En el extremo superior, La Molina llegó a registrar S/ 27,99, una de las cifras más elevadas de la comparación. La diferencia entre el menor y el mayor precio reportado fue de S/ 7,60 por galón. Sin embargo, elegir un combustible no debe depender únicamente del costo: los conductores tienen que respetar el octanaje recomendado por el fabricante de su vehículo para evitar problemas de rendimiento o funcionamiento del motor. El diésel B5 S-50 UV registró precios desde S/ 23,89 por galón en San Juan de Lurigancho y S/ 23,90 en Cieneguilla. En otros puntos de la capital, como Ancón, los valores llegaron a S/ 30,36. La diferencia entre establecimientos es especialmente relevante para transportistas, conductores de carga y trabajadores que dependen de este combustible para sus actividades. En cuanto al GLP y al GNV, los datos de referencia disponibles para Lima, actualizados durante la mañana del 18 de noviembre, situaron el GLP en un promedio de S/ 9,21 por galón y el GNV en S/ 1,70 por metro cúbico. Estas cifras corresponden a estaciones consideradas en el registro consultado y no representan una tarifa única para toda la ciudad: el precio final depende del grifo y de la disponibilidad del producto. Los usuarios pueden ingresar a la plataforma oficial Facilito de Osinergmin para comparar los precios de los combustibles en diferentes estaciones de servicio. El sistema permite seleccionar el departamento, la provincia y el distrito, además de identificar los establecimientos que ofrecen el producto requerido y consultar los valores que han reportado. Antes de abastecerse, es recomendable comprobar la fecha y hora de actualización de cada registro, así como verificar que el precio anunciado en la plataforma coincida con el que aparece en el surtidor. Los montos pueden cambiar durante el día y la disponibilidad también puede variar. Comparar alternativas cercanas permite tomar una mejor decisión sin realizar recorridos innecesarios que terminen consumiendo el ahorro esperado.

articles.title: Rafael López Aliaga a Jesús Gálvez: “Si quiere hablar, que no me bloquee (...) Estoy bloqueado por él”
articles.summary: El líder de Renovación Popular, Rafael López Aliaga, negó haber interrumpido el contacto con el tercer regidor electo de Lima por su partido, Jesús Gálvez, y dijo que es él quien lo mantiene bloqueado en WhatsApp. Sin embargo, justificó su pedido a Gálvez a para que renuncie a su militancia partidaria tras detectar aparentes contradicciones e irregularidades durante el reciente proceso electoral.
articles.body_text: El líder de Renovación Popular, Rafael López Aliaga, negó haber interrumpido el contacto con el tercer regidor electo de Lima por su partido, Jesús Gálvez, y dijo que es él quien lo mantiene bloqueado en WhatsApp. Sin embargo, justificó su pedido a Gálvez a para que renuncie a su militancia partidaria tras detectar aparentes contradicciones e irregularidades durante el reciente proceso electoral. “Para empezar, si quiere hablar, que no me bloquee (...) Le hemos enviado un mensaje ahorita y no hay manera que me responda. Le he enviado dos mensajes para hablar justamente y estoy bloqueado por él. Yo no le he bloqueado a él”, dijo este jueves al programa Beto a Saber de Willax TV. Acto siguiente, mostró su celular para mostrar que sus mensajes no eran recibidos por la otra parte. La declaración de López Aliaga respondió a las declaraciones que dio Gálvez en el programa “Siempre a las 8” de Jimmy Chinchay de El Comercio, en la que el también alcalde de Jesús María afirmó entre lágrimas haber sido apartado del partido mediante un mensaje de texto. En sus comentarios, dijo que se le pidió su renuncia sin oportunidad de dar sus descargos porque, según él, “había varios inconvenientes, hay información tergiversada que le debe haber llegado y que no hemos podido todavía aclarar”. Entre los argumentos expuestos, el dirigente enfatizó la postulación de Sergio Castromonte, excoordinador de proyectos de la Municipalidad de Jesús María bajo la gestión de Gálvez, a la alcaldía distrital de La Molina por una agrupación política rival. Según detalló López Aliaga, el candidato conocido como “el bombero” constituye un indicio de interferencia y respaldo a una candidatura que compitió de manera directa contra la postulación de Renovación Popular en dicho distrito. Un segundo cuestionamiento se relacionó con la falta de apoyo proselitista a favor del candidato distrital de Renovación Popular en Jesús María. Pese a que Gálvez ejercía como coordinador oficial del partido en esa jurisdicción, López Aliaga denunció la ausencia total de publicidad en este distrito. “En la distrital no ha habido un solo letrero, ni la cara ni el nombre del señor Lee, y el coordinador era Jesús Gálvez. Entonces le pregunto: ‘¿Por qué no ha habido un solo acto electoral, un solo acto de promoción?’. Cero respuesta, es lo que quiero conversar con él“. Asimismo, López Aliaga informó sobre la revisión en curso de cuatro contratos de iluminación ejecutados durante este año en el distrito de Jesús María. De acuerdo con el dirigente, las prestaciones de dicho servicio registrarían un presunto sobrecosto cercano a $1 millón. “Cuatro contratos que voy a investigar estarían inflados por casi un millón de dólares en Jesús María y que ese dinero habría ido a la campaña en La Molina, del ‘bombero’”. Finalmente, López Aliaga aseguró que el pedido de renuncia a Gálvez busca facilitar el desarrollo de las investigaciones internas sin incurrir en conflictos de interés. Añadió que la medida preventiva responde a un control de gestión posterior a los comicios para analizar el desempeño en cada circunscripción de la capital.

articles.title: Experts warn: Nearly everyone in AI is susceptible to a honey-trap scheme right now | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Techies are building technology that can advance all aspects of the world — but can they protect their hearts? That's the vulnerability that honey pots exploit.
articles.body_text: Even as the fall-out for Nvidia over Jensen Huang’s alleged honey-trap scandal is still unfolding, Silicon Valley has yet to reckon with a new reality: many more people among them are at risk. “Nobody briefs founders on counterintelligence,” Aaron Brown, a former senior CIA officer and current founder of the software company Lumbra, told TechCrunch. That’s because historically honey traps have been associated with politicians, the military, and national intelligence — the people “behind clearances and a workforce trained to expect an approach,” from spies and other attackers. But now many of the most valuable secrets “sit inside companies building chips, models, and infrastructure,” Brown says, adding that a spy “wants what the CEO can touch. The roadmap, the export decisions, the customer list, who gets the technology. The CEO is the shortest path to all of it.” Huang has been accused of falling for just such a honey trap by having an affair with Alice Huang. She’s a former executive of a Singapore neocloud who’s been accused of being a Chinese spy and of smuggling billions of dollars’ worth of restricted Nvidia chips into China. After the Huang allegations broke, jokes flooded the internet about which tech CEO will be next, but it’s not just CEOs and founders who are at risk. The WSJ reported that OpenAI started warning its employees about outsiders trying to cozy up to them in search of company secrets. Anyone with access to sensitive information — from board members to executive assistants — can be the target of a honey trap. And typically, the attackers aren’t lovers. Friendship is actually the oldest honey-trap scheme around, Brown said. Honey traps gain access to their targets as investors, customers, recruiters, and consultancies. Their requests look legitimate on paper and don’t need their targets to fall in love. “They need you to feel comfortable talking,” Brown said. “They last longer because nobody’s looking.” What’s interesting, too, is the irony. So many tech founders are moving to automate and digitize so much of human life and yet remain vulnerable to the oldest bug around, a person who preys on the human need to be understood by others. “Why fight through a firewall when you can get close to the person who can open doors, influence decisions, or make requests nobody wants to question?” Perry Carpenter, a criminologist and chief deception strategist at KnowBe4, told TechCrunch. Once targets realize they have been compromised, the threat can escalate: attackers now have a means of blackmail. Another irony: AI has made honey-trapping much easier and cheaper. Planning a scheme used to take months or years of research, crafting a persona, knowing the target, and executing a plan. These days, it’s easy to use AI to research a target, generate fake social profiles, fake backgrounds, even fake voice calls.

articles.title: Exclusive: Daniel Ek backs AI researcher's fusion power startup. Here's what they're building. | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Spotify founder Daniel Ek is backing Europa Fusion, a fusion power startup founded by an AI researcher. Here's what the startup is building.
articles.body_text: Spotify founder Daniel Ek is backing Europa Fusion, a stealthy fusion power startup founded by an AI researcher who is taking a different approach to developing a fusion power plant. The U.K.-based startup was founded in February, though sources told TechCrunch that the founder, Nantas Nardelli, has been working on the idea for longer. The people asked not to be identified because the information isn’t public. Bloomberg first reported Ek’s backing of Europa Fusion. Nardelli has extensive experience in the AI world, having previously worked at Google DeepMind, Facebook AI Research, and Microsoft Research Cambridge. Recently, he was head of machine learning at Pacific Fusion , the fusion power startup based in Fremont, California. Pacific Fusion recently broke ground on a demonstration facility in New Mexico. Like most fusion startups of its size , Pacific Fusion leans heavily on physical devices to test its theories and improve its simulations. Nardelli apparently didn’t agree with the focus on hardware, instead thinking that fusion startups should invest in a more simulation- and data-heavy approach, a source familiar with his thinking told TechCrunch. Like Pacific Fusion, Europa Fusion will pursue a pulsed-power approach to fusion. Pulsed-power reactors use massive, perfectly timed surges of electrical current to compress fuel targets until the atoms inside fuse and release energy. Fusion power has the potential to be a significant energy source in the coming decades, but to date, no one has built a power plant capable of supplying electricity to the grid. If fusion power becomes commercially viable, though, it could possibly be a significant source of carbon-free power that draws on nearly limitless fuel supplies. The technology also has the potential to alleviate concerns about AI’s energy consumption. Fusion’s ability to generate electricity without exacerbating climate change apparently drove Nardelli’s pivot from AI. “My original background is in electronics and control engineering,” he wrote on his website . “I used to build robots for a living. One day I’ll be back to that, but it’s time to fix climate change for good.” When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: AI claimed a solution to the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis — and a human did, too | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Mathematicians are having their minds blown by the latest AI-driven result — and there's a competing human solution, too.
articles.body_text: It’s a big week for Levent Alpöge: The mathematician saw his employer, Anthropic, become the first publicly traded frontier AI lab. He also appears to have solved one of the most important problems in mathematics. “The precise timing is horrible,” he wrote in an essay announcing his findings and describing how he messaged Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei last Sunday night to ask how to announce that he had found a Lean-compilable solution to the Riemann hypothesis, which dates back to 1859 and is among the Millennium Prize math problems. The hypothesis conjectures that there is a hidden structure underlying the appearance of prime numbers. If the claimed result holds true, we’re entering sublime-mysteries-of-the-universe territory. Maybe the best way to understand how exciting this is to the mathematics community is to watch the experts puzzling through the result in a chat on Zulip . Mathematicians like Chris Birkbeck, a number theorist at the University of East Anglia, are posting thoughts like this … The cohomology bound is proved by what looks like an automorphy-lifting argument. It genuinely uses the existence of Galois representations attached to regular algebraic, polarized cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_n over CM fields, along with base change, Jacquet–Shalika, Clozel’s purity, Bernstein–Zelevinsky, the main theorem of CM, Deligne–Ribet and more. For my part, I tapped out of mathematics at college calculus, so I can’t help decode exactly what that means. But that comment was followed by 20 readers reacting 🤯. It will be a while before the mathematics community feels like it has a handle on the proof, but most appear confident that the formalized Lean result will hold. Lean is an an open-source coding language used to express mathematical ideas as code, allowing proofs to be formally verified. Several participants in the Zulip chat, including MIT mathematician Andrew Sutherland, say they have successfully confirmed that Alpöge’s solution can be compiled successfully. Alpöge appeared in his essay to feel a bit guilty about releasing the proof without a truly human-intelligible explanation, but his obsession with the problem since childhood made him feel he “could not live” if he waited to release the finding. Alpöge described a “stream-of-consciousness jaunt through the experience of finding all the pieces of the argument through incredible confusion with Claude” with more than a hint of AI euphoria, describing how the model “flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line.” However, for all that action to mean anything, we’ll have to wait for humans to be able to understand the result and explain it to each other, something Alpöge has committed to pursue. Alpöge and a collaborator, NYU mathematician Tristan Buckmaster, also released another important proof related to the Navier-Stokes equations, problems that helped kick off the race between frontier labs and mathematicians to solve outstanding problems this summer.

articles.title: Super-hot rock geothermal could end data center energy woes | TechCrunch
articles.summary: New geothermal startups are betting that they can leapfrog today's leaders to deliver terawatts of electricity nearly anywhere.
articles.body_text: Geothermal startups are in a race to see who can tap the deepest, hottest rocks. The winners could power the next phase of the grid, data centers and all. The broader markets got their first taste of enhanced geothermal earlier this year when Fervo Energy went public. But this week was all about super-hot rock geothermal. Geothermal has become a darling among investors, tech companies, and even the Trump administration. The basic technology has been around for decades, but advances in drilling techniques borrowed from the oil and gas industry has supercharged it. The U.S. has plenty of potential, too, with up to 57 terawatts of generating capacity, more than enough to power the next wave of AI data centers. An emerging class of geothermal energy, known as super-hot rock, could help the industry unlock much of that potential. The secret to super-hot rock geothermal is what happens to water at extreme depths. As it gets closer to the superheated core of the Earth, both temperature and pressure rise significantly. When they get high enough, ordinary water turns into a supercritical fluid — a sort of gaseous-liquid state that can carry tremendous amounts of energy. A single super-hot rock well could generate 15 megawatts of electricity or more. Super-hot rock geothermal is inching closer to commercial reality. Quaise Energy said on Tuesday that it had landed Google as a customer. The hyperscaler said it would pay more than $500 million to secure 50 megawatts of power from a Quaise project in central Oregon, which will tap into searing heat three miles deep. Google is paying a premium for the amount of power Quaise will deliver, but that’s in line with the company’s strategy of getting in early with potential suppliers. For instance, it was an investor in and an early customer of Fervo. Meanwhile, on Monday, Khosla-backed Mazama Energy announced it had figured out how to keep its drill heads cool as they tap into super-hot rocks. And last week, XGS Energy was given a grant by the Department of Energy to develop and refine materials, well designs, and models to improve reliability at depths where super-hot rock exists. XGS is dipping its toes in the super-hot waters, while Mazama and Quaise have made it their core focus, though they’re taking very different approaches. Quaise’s technology sounds like science fiction: Starting at about 2.5 miles deep, the company will swap out its conventional drill bit for one powered by a gyrotron, bombarding rock with millimeter-wave radiation and turning it into ash. The hope is that the technology can make drilling under super-hot conditions cost-effective, something that’s challenging with traditional metal drill bits, which wear out faster at those temperatures. Mazama, on the other hand, thinks that traditional drill bits will work just fine if they can be kept cool. The startup’s newly announced technology, Carbon Chill, uses carbon dioxide in place of water-based drilling “mud” to keep the bit cool. At those depths and temperatures, the carbon dioxide turns supercritical, allowing it to hold significant amounts of energy. Just above the drill bit, the CO 2 flows through a valve that looks similar to a rocket nozzle. As the gas flows through the valve and expands on the other end, the expansion rapidly cools it, allowing it to absorb significant amounts of heat. The CO 2 also removes drill cuttings on its trip to the surface, where it’s filtered and reused.

articles.title: Chips can survive the space environment — can their financing? | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Lenders don't want SpaceX shooting their collateral into orbit. What does that mean for space data centers writ large?
articles.body_text: The push to build data centers in space faces plenty of obstacles, from tricky engineering to a dearth of rockets that could take chips to orbit. But what about paying for the chips? The data center ecosystem currently depends on debt financing, with cloud providers borrowing to build out data centers and then paying back the loans with a share of the revenue. Those deals typically use the chips as collateral — if the data centers default on their loans, the lenders can take possession of the chips and resell them. That backstop makes it cheaper for companies to finance their chips. Even older chips retain value — according to Compute Credit Index Research , some H100s are selling for about half of their original cost basis from 2023, while some H200 configurations are selling for the same price they did when introduced in 2024. But you’re not going to repossess chips installed in a satellite orbiting 300 miles above Earth at 17,500 miles per hour. The Financial Times is reporting that lenders behind SpaceX’s $40 billion chip financing deal asked that none of the chips purchased be used for the company’s orbital data center plans. It’s not clear if they succeeded in getting SpaceX to agree with the provision. That may not matter to the company in the near term — SpaceX’s ability to deploy compute at terrestrial ground stations has proven lucrative, and on the company’s most recent earnings call, CEO Elon Musk detailed how he was dispatching engineers from the company’s rocket team to accelerate that build-out by taking on challenges like casting turbine blades for generators at faster than existing suppliers. However, open questions remain about how easy it will be to find land and power to support the data center build-out. Many potential projects face delays and local opposition, while markets wait to see the state of compute demand and the ability of its buyers to turn it into revenue. Musk, meanwhile, began saying at the beginning of 2026 that he believes space will be the “cheapest” place to operate data centers in two to three years. That’s unlikely until SpaceX can fly its Starship rocket in a fully reusable configuration. In its most recent flight test, the company failed to recover the booster stage but did succeed in landing the orbital stage of the rocket back at its launch facility in Texas. It’s not clear, though, when the second stage will fly again or how expensive it will be to prepare it for a second trip to space. Even with Starship, however, SpaceX — as well as startups like StarCloud, Cowboy Space Corporation, Sophia Space, Orbital, and others — will need to buy chips. If the already daunting economics of space data centers weren’t challenging enough, it looks like they’ll be spending more to buy them than their terrestrial counterparts. That might be an advantage for Google, which is focused on deploying its own TPU chips in space through Project Suncatcher. SpaceX and Tesla are working together to build their own chip foundry, Terafab, in the U.S., but that project has yet to break ground and will require years and billions of dollars before it starts producing semiconductors at scale. articles.title: Bending Spoons buys Mailchimp for $3.68B | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Intuit acquired the company in 2021 for roughly $12 billion, so it looks like Bending Spoons is getting quite a bargain.
articles.body_text: Bending Spoons has bought up another distressed internet company. This time, it’s the email marketing firm Mailchimp, bought for $3.68 billion from the tax-preparation giant Intuit. Intuit acquired the company in 2021 for roughly $12 billion, so it’s taking quite a loss — and, perhaps, Bending Spoons is getting quite a bargain. At the time of the sale to Intuit, that acquisition caused headlines because Mailchimp employees reportedly received no equity, so no share of the sale proceeds, because the founders had allegedly promised them they didn’t need it as they would never sell. Flash forward to now, with Intuit hit hard by the Death Star to SaaS trade — aka AI — with the company’s shares worth less than half what they were a year ago. The company told Reuters that the sale will let it sharpen its focus on AI tools for small businesses, and the new cash will be used to repurchase shares. Bending Spoons describes the transaction as an all-cash deal, although that’s not quite true: As part of the same package, Intuit is buying $368 million in newly minted shares of Bending Spoons, so the net effect is a split of 90% cash to 10% stock. Still, the transaction is a major pickup for Bending Spoons, which has become a kind of clearinghouse for late-stage web properties, with its game plan to hold them long term. In just the last year, the company has snapped up AOL, Eventbrite, Airtable, and Miro . Previous acquisitions include older stalwarts like Evernote, Meetup, and Vimeo. In each case, Bending Spoons integrated the products into centralized engineering and revenue systems, resulting in significant cost savings while often improving the available support and product resources. “We want to place ourselves as an operator that takes beloved brands and makes them much better,” Bending Spoons co-founder and chief product officer, Matteo Danieli, told TechCrunch in July . articles.title: A transcription firm used by police, prosecutors, and tech giants exposed customer data online | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Exclusive: A simple security lapse exposed transcriptions of police interviews and bodycam footage on a cloud server without a password.
articles.body_text: A transcription company that caters to law enforcement, government departments, and Silicon Valley tech giants has resolved a security lapse after leaving a large amount of internal data, including customer transcriptions and their source materials, exposed to the web. The data security lapse at San Francisco-based Tigerfish exposed transcriptions of police interviews, body-cam footage, and customers’ raw audio and video footage. The exposed data also included invoices of the company’s customers, which include police departments and prosecutors’ offices. According to Anurag Sen , a good faith security researcher who found the data, the files were located on an Amazon-hosted (S3) cloud server that was openly listed and accessible to anyone via an easy-to-guess web address — no passwords needed. The security lapse underscores how simple flaws or misconfigurations can result in sensitive information getting exposed online, especially as AI makes it easier to uncover weaknesses that can put companies and their data at risk. Sen discovered the exposed data online in October and alerted the company to the issue, but did not hear back. Sen later provided details to TechCrunch in an effort to flag the incident with the company for resolution. Sen, 30, is no stranger to TechCrunch. For the past decade, he has searched for sensitive datasets exposed online with the goal of notifying the companies and organizations that their information is open to the internet. Like many security researchers, much of his efforts are driven by a duty to secure the internet, and he describes his work as an “unpaid air-traffic controller.” From his island home in Indonesia, Sen has uncovered sensitive U.S. military emails spilling from a compartmentalized Department of Defense cloud server; databases exposing reams of customer records ; the inner workings of a country’s national license plate surveillance system ; and public systems that inadvertently sent out streams of SMS codes used by people around the world to log into their online accounts. Given Sen’s propensity for finding often highly confidential information online, we verified the source of the leak and the data, and contacted Tigerfish. Soon after making contact, Tigerfish secured its exposed S3 cloud bucket. “We’ve blocked all public access to the bucket you identified, including directory listings and individual files,” Tigerfish president, Adam Goldberg, said in an email. “We’ve also verified that all of our other S3 buckets are blocked to public access.” “We’re continuing to review and strengthen our storage security more broadly,” added Goldberg. The company said that Sen’s email disclosing the data leak was caught in its spam filter.

articles.title: Six AI-powered gadgets that could make your home office smarter | TechCrunch
articles.summary: From notetakers to webcams, here are six AI-powered gadgets to upgrade your workspace.
articles.body_text: Tech companies are racing to figure out how AI can make everyday work a little easier. From notetakers to webcams that follow your movements, here are six AI-powered gadgets worth checking out if you want to upgrade your workspace. If you’re constantly scribbling notes during meetings, the Flowtica Scribe could save you from having to type everything up afterward. The AI-powered pen combines traditional handwriting with audio recording. You can use its built-in gel pen to take notes, tap the side to highlight important points, and press the end of the pen to start recording audio. Once the meeting is over, its AI can transcribe the conversation, summarize key takeaways, and create a to-do list based on what was discussed. You can even ask the AI questions about the meeting to find specific information without having to go through the entire recording. The Scribe comes with a built-in microphone and 32GB of onboard storage. It can also identify up to 15 different speakers and supports 92 languages. Anker’s AI-powered recording pin, Soundcore Work , is designed to capture conversations, meetings, and quick voice memos without taking up much space on your desk. Priced at $159 (currently reduced to $99 in the Amazon Black Friday sale), the coin-sized device comes with a puck-shaped charging case and can record for up to eight hours on a single charge, extending to 32 hours when used with its case. Anker also claims a recording range of up to 5 meters, making it useful for capturing conversations around a meeting table. The companion app handles transcription and uses AI to turn recordings into more organized notes and summaries. Users also get 300 minutes of free audio transcription each month. If you need more recording capacity or access to additional AI features, Anker offers optional subscription plans, including Pro ($99 per year) and Unlimited ($239 per year). Logitech’s MX Keypad brings AI shortcuts directly to your desk, with dedicated buttons that let you launch your preferred AI assistant or trigger specific productivity tools with a single press. If you frequently switch between different apps and AI assistants, having these shortcuts within reach could make your workday easier. The keypad can be configured to work with tools such as GitHub Copilot and Claude Code, along with a range of popular productivity and creative apps, such as OpenAI Codex, Microsoft Teams, PowerPoint, Excel, Notion, Slack, Photoshop, Final Cut Pro, Zoom, and Figma.

articles.title: Behind Jensen Huang’s exit, questions about a management style reportedly built on fear | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Elon Musk may have been overstating it when he said Nvidia’s employees “love” the ousted Jensen Huang.
articles.body_text: Earlier this week at the DealBook conference in New York, Elon Musk, beamed in from a trip to China with President Donald Trump, was asked about the ouster of his longtime friend, former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Musk compared it to kicking Michael Jordan off the Chicago Bulls’ roster during his historic run. Of Nvidia’s employees, he said, “They love [Huang]. They love him.” Well, maybe not all of them. Thousands of employees have signed a letter asking for Huang’s return, but others tell The New York Times he ruled through praise and fear, as well as by humiliating people. According to the Times, Huang told subordinates that Nvidia’s wealth meant it wasn’t possible to motivate employees with money, so humiliation was the only lever left. He reportedly told one executive his mother should have aborted him and told another employee he would rip his arms off and beat him to death with them. Naturally, over a 33-year career, regrettable things may have been said, but the Times found a long paper trail that suggests the incidents weren’t isolated. In 2005, for example, Michael Winston, a former HR chief, threatened to sue and called Huang’s conduct the most abusive he’d seen. Nvidia paid him more than $1 million. Huang’s spokesman calls the allegations fabrications. Every weekday and Sunday, you can get the best of TechCrunch’s coverage. articles.title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explains why he asked 60K employees to quit | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explained why he offered buyouts to 60,000 of his employees in October, essentially urging them to voluntarily quit, rather than reducing the workforce via another massive layoff. The short answer is AI, but not in the way you might expect.
articles.body_text: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explained Wednesday why he offered buyouts to 60,000 of his employees in October, essentially urging them to voluntarily quit instead of reducing the workforce via another massive layoff. Short answer: AI, but not, he insists, in the way you might expect. He’s not saying he’s replacing employees with AI, especially software engineers. He’s saying he’s reorganizing Microsoft into a company where everyone uses AI to do their work, and their jobs become focused on managing that AI. The buyout was “to make sure that at least everyone felt like they had agency in making choices,” he told Andrew Ross Sorkin during the DealBook Summit. “Let’s take software engineering. We went from, ‘Well, we don’t buy that AI can ever do software.’ To suddenly, ‘Wow, it can do all software, and why do we need software engineers?’ To now rediscovering that software engineering is very much alive and, in fact, is going to thrive, except the way the team is organized and the work that a software engineer does has now got a new operating point,” he explained. For some people, “that reorganization and change is sort of hard, right?” he added, “but, I mean, it has to be done.” He offered the example of the team that builds Cowork, the AI agent in Microsoft 365 apps. He said the team consists of just 11 developers who have mastered using AI to do their jobs. “They build a software factory that builds the product. They don’t build the product.” He believes that every employee will one day similarly become a manager of agents, rather than a person directly doing the work. “That level of direction is what, by the way, is going to happen in all jobs.” But Microsoft, as a 51-year-old company, didn’t grow up as an AI-first company. “So the question is, how quickly can an incumbent transform the work, the workflow, and the work artifact, and with all the wage support that goes with it?” he said. “It’s going to take a bit more time than anyone expects. And there is going to be in all of this, you know, people who may say, ‘Hey, I have some other choices I want to make.’” When asked about this same topic — why ask 60,000 people to voluntarily resign — last week by Gergely Orosz on his The Pragmatic Engineer podcast , Nadella further explained, “We have created enormous anxiety in people sort of feeling that they don’t have control of their own destiny because the way we have talked about this AI revolution.” He called out talk about the singularity (the hypothetical point at which AI surpasses human intelligence) and predictions that AI will take away all jobs. “All of that leads anyone who even wants to change to be sort of anxious … You have to sort of walk the hard walk of really making the structural changes, getting people slotted, giving them opportunity.” In other words, the buyout was the message to employees: You can get with the new AI-first program, which will radically change your job, or you choose to get on with your life. articles.summary: Den före detta prins Andrew riskerar åtal nästa år. Då kommer han sannolikt fly till Mellanöstern. Det tror kungliga experten Andrew Lownie.
articles.body_text: Den före detta prins Andrew riskerar åtal nästa år. Då kommer han sannolikt fly till Mellanöstern. Det tror kungliga experten Andrew Lownie. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Andrew Mountbatten-Windsoor, tidigare prins Andrew, greps i februari för tjänstefel. Misstankarna har sin grund i hans kopplingar till pedofilmiljardären Jeffrey Epstein . Den förra kungligheten släpptes snabbt, men misstankarna mot honom kvarstår. – Jag står i kontakt med polisen och jag tror att åtalet kommer nästa år, säger den kungliga experten Andrew Lownie till Daily Mail . Lownie är författaren bakom skandalbiografin ”Entitled: The Rise And Fall Of The House Of York”, en bok om Andrews och hans exhustru Sarah Fergusons förehavanden. Han säger att han den senaste tiden stärkts i sin tro att åtalet är på gång. – De verkar ha många nya spår, saker som inte är offentliga ännu, säger Lownie, som påpekar att det i förlängningen inte bara handlar om tjänstefel utan även om trafficking och andra saker. – Kungafamiljen kommer inte vilja inte ha honom i vittnesbåset, så jag tror att det är ganska sannolikt att han helt enkelt lämnar landet i hemlighet och tar sig till Mellanöstern. articles.body_text: Trumpadministrationen har offentliggjort material om Bigfoot. Efter årtionden av tystnad släpps tre dokument om den mytiska figuren. Det första dokumentet handlar om en utredning 1982 av några misstänkta spår i Oregon. ”Min bedömning är att spåren som observerades... gjordes av något annat än en tvåbent varelse på uppåt 140 kilo”, skriver biologen som utredde saken. Nästa är ett tidningsutklipp från Clark Fork Valley Press i Montana, där några personer berättar om spår i snön som såg mer mänskliga än djuriska ut. – Jag vet inte om jag tror på Bigfoot-teorin, men spåren var ju där, säger en man vid namn Bob Mesing. Han och Dean Petersen följde spåren i uppåt två timmar och hittade hundratals, men de försvann när det blev mindre snö på marken inne i skogen. Något odjur fick de aldrig se. Även det tredje gäller en observation i Montana. Den här gången på 1940-talet. En jägare berättade att han hittat en stor mängd spår som ledde bort från ett hjortkadaver. – Först gissade vi på att det var en stor björn, men björnar går bara korta sträckor på bakbenen och skulle normalt ha släpat med sig ett så stort kadaver, sa jägaren. Samtidigt har ett möte, ”Bigfoot in Your Backyard”, anordnats vid Stanislaus national forest nära Yosemite.

articles.title: Oväntade svaret – på frågan om valet
articles.summary: JD Vance eller Marco Rubio som Trumps efterträdare? För presidenten tycks svaret vara någon helt annan. – Han var bättre än de här två killarna, säger han vid en pressträff.
articles.body_text: JD Vance eller Marco Rubio som Trumps efterträdare? För presidenten tycks svaret vara någon helt annan. – Han var bättre än de här två killarna, säger han vid en pressträff. Vem ska efterträda honom som presidentkandidat för det republikanska partiet? För många har det givna svaret varit vicepresident JD Vance. För andra har det varit utrikesminister Marco Rubio. Alla har dock varit överens om att det är presidenten som kommer att vara kungamakare – och han har inte sagt något om vem han föredrar. På fredagen höll Donald Trump en pressträff med både Vance och Rubio bakom sig och föreställningen blev nästan som ett avsnitt i ”The Apprentice”. De båda eventuella kandidaterna utbytte blickar och miner vid flera tillfällen samtidigt som presidenten orerade. Vance har kämpat i motvind sedan republikanernas förnedring i mellanårsvalet och sin efterföljande analys av orsaken, där han – förmodligen till stor del med rätta – la skulden på kriget i Iran. En reporter frågade om kriget var värt det, även om det orsakade förlorad kontroll över senaten. Svaret blev något svävande. – Presidenten har sagt att han skulle göra om det. Mitt jobb är att stödja USA:s president. Vance skämtade också om att ha blivit kvarlämnad hemma när Trump och Rubio besökte Filippinerna och Kina. – Det var lite som i 'Ensam hemma', fast med bättre mat och mer guld. Så, jag saknade er, sa han i riktning mot presidenten. Rubio var mer allvarsam och förklarade hur viktig resan var och hyllade Trump för hans möten med Xi och Putin.

articles.title: Man döms för sadistmordet på Sonia, 32
articles.summary: Sonia Exelby kom till USA för att bli mördad av en man hon träffade på en fetischsajt. Hon ångrade sig – men mördades ändå. Nu döms Dwain Hall, 54, till livstids fängelse för mordet.
articles.body_text: Sonia Exelby kom till USA för att bli mördad av en man hon träffade på en fetischsajt. Nu döms Dwain Hall, 54, till livstids fängelse för mordet. Musikläraren Sonia Exelby, 32, hade sedan länge haft psykiska besvär när hon började chatta med den amerikanska bilmekanikern Dwain Hall på en fetischsajt. Han, en sadist som dyrkar den egyptiska dödsguden Anubis, groomade den sårbara brittiska kvinnan i två år. I chattar, där han kallade sig ”Alpha Sadist”, utnyttjade han hennes kamp mot depression och bipolaritet för att kunna uppfylla sina egna fantasier. Han uppmuntrade hennes självmordstankar och manipulerade henne till att tro att hon ville bli torterad och mördad, och erbjöd sig att ta ”uppdraget” för 4 000 dollar – ett erbjudande hon ska ha gått med på. Enligt utredningen förde hon också över 1 200 dollar till Hall. I oktober förra året flög hon från sitt hem i Portsmouth till Florida för en resa som skulle avsluta hennes liv. Redan på flyget blev det tydligt att hon ångrade sig. ”Så fort hjulen lämnar marken ... Jag önskar att jag var hemma, men jag kan inte ta mig av planet, det är redan i rörelse” , skrev hon i ett mejl till sig själv som The Telegraph citerar. ”Jag har gjort bort mig något för jävligt.” Ändå fortsatte hon. Hon följde med Hall till ett avlägset hus som hon hyrt på Airbnb. Dagen därpå skrev hon meddelanden på sociala medier till en vän. Det var tydligt att tortyren hade börjat. Han ska ha sagt till henne att hennes enda utväg är att ta pistolen han bär på och skjuta honom. ”Jag trodde inte att jag skulle bli rädd. Jag trodde att han skulle göra det snabbt och inte ge mig tid att älta och inse att det här är det sista jag någonsin säger till någon”, skriver hon.

articles.title: Glömde föremål i patientens huvud
articles.summary: Efter en hjärnoperation i Umeå glömdes två föremål kvar i patienten huvud. De upptäcktes dagar senare på en röntgen och tolkades då som blödningar.
articles.body_text: Under en hjärnoperation i Umeå glömdes två föremål kvar i patientens huvud. De upptäcktes först efter han opererats igen. – Det här var en beklaglig och olycklig händelse, säger chefläkaren Bengt Andersson till SVT Nyheter Västerbotten . Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. I augusti kom mannen i 55-årsåldern till Norrlands universitetssjukhus i Umeå för att operera bort en hjärntumör. Två dagar senare var han på återbesök och hans huvud röntgades. Då upptäcktes något som först tolkades som en blödning inne i skallen. På grund av det tvingades mannen genomgå ytterligare en hjärnoperation. Först då upptäckte man att det rörde sig om två kompresser som kirurgerna glömt kvar i huvudet efter operationen, rapporterar SVT Nyheter Västerbotten . En kompress är en tygbit av gasväv som används för att torka eller suga upp vätska under operationer. Chefläkaren på sjukhuset, Bengt Andersson säger att kompresserna inte innehåller röntgentät tråd och att de därför inte upptäcktes under röntgenundersökningen. Sjukvården anser att patienten utsattes för en risk för allvarlig skada. Han ska ha återhämtat sig väl efter de två ingreppen. Händelsen har nu anmälts enligt lex Maria och har utretts av sjukhuset. De har nu ändrat sina rutiner. – Rutinen var inte komplett. Förut låg ansvaret enbart hos kirurgen, nu står det att även operationssköterskan ska räkna kompresserna, säger Bengt Andersson till kanalen.

articles.title: Ai-bossen anklagas för brutalt skräckvälde
articles.summary: Jensen Huang ska ha hotat slita huvudet av en anställd – och sagt till en annan att hans mamma borde ha gjort abort. Nvidias förra vd anklagas nu för ett riktigt skräckvälde. Enligt New York Times pågick det i decennier.
articles.body_text: Jensen Huang ska ha hotat slita huvudet av en anställd – och sagt till en annan att hans mamma borde ha gjort abort. Nvidias förra vd anklagas nu för ett riktigt skräckvälde. Jensen Huang var med och bildade Nvidia 1993, och när han avgick förra veckan hade han varit techbolagets vd i över 30 år. Men han styrde genom fruktan, skriver New York Times . Enligt tidningen, som hänvisar till dokument och intervjuer, har han i åratal skällt ut sina anställda på ”brutala” och ”uppfinningsrika” sätt. Och ju mer framgångsrikt Nvidia blev, desto mer frustrerad ska Huang ha blivit på personalen. Han ska ha sagt till anställda att de blivit så rika att han inte längre kunde motivera dem med pengar, utan behövde använda förnedring. En chef fick, enligt NYT, höra att hans mamma borde ha gjort abort. En annan anställd ska Jensen Huang ha hotat att slita huvudet av, för att sen pissa på den anställdas hjärna. Ytterligare en anställd ska vd:n ha sagt att han skulle slita armarna av, för att sen använda dem till att slå personen i huvudet tills personen dog. NYT beskriver utbrotten som ett ”centralt inslag” i kulturen på Nvidia, och som ”grundläggande” för Huangs ledarstil. Det ska ha nått HR-avdelningen på bolaget, men enligt uppgifter tog avdelningen inte klagomålen på allvar.

articles.title: HR-chefen jobbar från Costa del Sol
articles.summary: Kommunens HR-chef väljer spanska solkusten före Österåker. Genom ”en särskild överenskommelse” tillåts hon jobba distans från Costa del sol.
articles.body_text: Österåkers HR-chef Malin Hansson väljer spanska solkusten före Åkersberga. Genom ”en särskild överenskommelse” tillåts hon jobba på distans från Costa del Sol. – När jag är inne och rör mig får jag samma känsla som om jag hade varit här exakt varje dag, säger hon till Nu Österåker Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. I flera av Sveriges kommuner och regioner tillåts inte medarbetare att jobba på distans utanför landets gränser. Men i Österåkers kommun har HR-chefen Malin Hansson fått ett unikt upplägg. Majoriteten av sitt arbete gör hon från den spanska solkusten, rapporterar Nu Österåker . Det upplägget har hon haft i två år. Enligt avtalet ska HR-chefen vara på plats i Österåker i genomsnitt var tredje vecka. – Vi försöker vara en modern och attraktiv arbetsgivare. Jag tittar på resultatet och det har mindre betydelse för mig var personen är bosatt. Vi vill ha det bästa för medarbetarna, säger kommunchefen Staffan Erlandsson om upplägget. Han menar att deras säkerhetssystem och program gör det möjligt att jobba ”från Norrtälje eller längre distanser”. Han säger att Malin Hansson har ett av de högsta värdena i kommunens medarbetarundersökningar. Hon beskriver själv deras upplägg som friktionsfritt. – När jag är inne och rör mig får jag samma känsla som om jag hade varit här exakt varje dag. Jag ser ingen skillnad på det, säger Malin Hansson och fortsätter: – Tempen på en arbetsplats kan man ta på flera andra sätt än att ses fysiskt. articles.title: Pourmokhtari starkt kritisk till avtalsförslaget
articles.summary: Klimattoppmötet COP 31 drar ut på tiden. Man kommer inte överens. I det senaste avtalsförslaget utelämnas ordet ”fossil”. – Det är ett katastrofalt förslag som kommer från det turkiska och australienska ordförandeskapet, säger klimat- och miljöminister Romina Pourmokhtari (L).
articles.body_text: Klimattoppmötet COP 31 drar ut på tiden. I det senaste avtalsförslaget utelämnas ordet ”fossil”. – Det är ett katastrofalt förslag som kommer från det turkiska och australienska ordförandeskapet, säger klimat- och miljöminister Romina Pourmokhtari (L). Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Toppmötet skulle tagit slut på fredagen, men det är långt från avslutat. I det avtal som ligger på bordet nämner man inte fossila bränslen, något som Sveriges klimat- och miljöminister är starkt kritisk till. – Man vill fortsätta att prata om finansiering i all evighet, men vad är det vi ska finansiera om inte insatser för att ställa om bort från fossila bränslen? säger hon i Aktuellt . Enligt henne är det Sverige och Frankrike som är de länder som varit allra hårdast i att inte ”gå med på vad som helst.” Hon önskar skrivningar med tydligt fokus på omställning till ren energi och att vi ska bort från de fossila bränslena. – Är det så att de här förhandlingarna kraschar så är det mycket på grund av att man vägrar nämna själva grunden till global uppvärmning och det är därför vi är här. Jag är inte här för en energikonferens, jag är inte här för att prata om kol, olja och gas. Jag är här för att ställa om, bort från fossila bränslen. Hon säger att hon förstår att det är lätt att tappa hoppet kring klimatarbetet och att det finns länder med starka intressen i att sprida bilden att det är Europa som är bromskloss och inte vill betala. – Nu sätter vi allt hopp till kommissionen och Irland som leder EU, men också till ordförandeskapet, Australien och Turkiet. De måste visa vägen, blir det nya rena mål eller blir det ord på papper? Den svenska delegationen har tippat på när mötet avslutas. Klimat- och miljöminister tror lördag 21.18. FN:s årliga klimattoppmöte kallas för COP (Conference of the Parties).
